items_all.title: Inception 扩散模型 Mercury 3 上线 OpenRouter
items_all.summary: Inception 的扩散模型 Mercury 3 上线 OpenRouter，生成速度超 1,000 tok/s，支持 1M 上下文，是 Mercury 2.5 的 4 倍。Inception 报告其在 IFBench、GPQA Diamond 和 SWE-Bench Atlas 上超过 GPT-6 Luna 和 Haiku 5.5；上线期五折，价格 $0.10/M 输入、$0.35/M 输出。

items_all.title_en: Mercury 3 is live on OpenRouter!
items_all.title_zh: Inception 扩散模型 Mercury 3 上线 OpenRouter

en.summary: Inception's diffusion model Mercury 3 is now live on OpenRouter, with generation speeds over 1,000 tok/s, 1M context support, and 4x the speed of Mercury 2.5. Inception reports it beats GPT-6 Luna and Haiku 5.5 on IFBench, GPQA Diamond, and SWE-Bench Atlas; launch pricing is 50% off at $0.10/M input and $0.35/M output.

items_all.title: Meta 详解 Thin Orchestrator 模式：让路由少干活提升 AI 智能体可靠性
items_all.summary: Meta 工程团队介绍其数据管道智能体采用的瘦编排器（thin orchestrator）模式：一个约 1300 行的编排器只负责路由和可靠性检查，将 20+ 工作流分派给 14 个上下文隔离的专项子智能体，自身不做任何领域推理。

items_all.title_en: The Thin Orchestrator: How We Made Our AI Agents More Reliable by Giving the Router Less to Do

en.summary: Meta's engineering team describes the thin orchestrator pattern behind its data pipeline agents: a roughly 1,300-line orchestrator handles only routing and reliability checks, dispatching 20+ workflows to 14 context-isolated specialist sub-agents while performing no domain reasoning itself.

items_all.title: Numan 如何用 LangGraph 和 LangSmith 构建评测优先的 AI 健康教练 Nu
items_all.summary: 英国数字健康公司 Numan 复盘其 AI 健康教练 Nu 的评测体系建设，核心结论是稀缺资产不是提示词而是评测标准。单轮静态数据集和脚本化多轮对话都难以覆盖真实会话，Nu 改为按类别打分的主题数据集、以更廉价模型扮演患者的模拟对话层，并让安全回归自动阻断发布。
items_all.title_original: How Numan Built an Eval-First AI Health Coach with LangGraph and LangSmith
items_all.title_en: How Numan Built an Eval-First AI Health Coach with LangGraph and LangSmith
items_all.title_zh: Numan 如何用 LangGraph 和 LangSmith 构建评测优先的 AI 健康教练 Nu
items_all.title_bilingual: Numan 如何用 LangGraph 和 LangSmith 构建评测优先的 AI 健康教练 Nu / How Numan Built an Eval-First AI Health Coach with LangGraph and LangSmith

en.summary: UK digital health company Numan has reflected on building the evaluation system for its AI health coach Nu, concluding that the scarce asset is not prompts but evaluation standards. Single-turn static datasets and scripted multi-turn dialogues struggle to cover real conversations, so Nu moved to topic datasets scored by category, a simulated-dialogue layer where cheaper models play patients, and automated blocking of releases when safety regressions occur.

en.summary: This week's AI music newsletter covers new copyright rules, several major product updates, and cutting-edge academic papers. YouTube Music has added AI music labeling, and major record labels have filed lawsuits, offering music creators clear compliance reminders. A range of practical audio tools also received concentrated updates, including a portable guitar workstation, video sound effect generation, a team music collaboration suite, and a local open-source production solution.

en.summary: This article traces the full technical evolution from the original Transformer to the rise of Decoder-only as the mainstream, breaking down the differences among major model architectures. It may help you clarify where model selection boundaries lie and quickly determine whether an automation task calls for a generative large model or a specialized decision model.

Ideal for LLM beginners looking to build a complete knowledge framework.

en.summary: Lovart 2.0 has launched Arti, a personal design Agent that remembers your aesthetic style and layout habits, so new projects no longer require re-entering prompts. It comes with canvas inspection that automatically catches visual bugs, supports in-canvas collaborative annotations, aggregates requests and applies revisions in one click, and can set up scheduled design commissions that automatically produce assets at each milestone. As your body of work grows, it increasingly aligns with your creative thinking, efficiently handling batch design work such as brand visuals and cultural and creative posters.

en.summary: The mysterious rabbit Space Bunny that took the developer world by storm has turned out to be MiniMax M3.1 Flash. During its anonymous phase it carried over 200T tokens of traffic and has long held the top spot on the OpenCode usage leaderboard. The new version is nearly 3x faster at inference and cuts overall Agent costs by 70%, closing in on flagship models across evaluations for office automation, coding, and computer use. It offers flexible switching across multiple inference effort levels, affordable API pricing, and its weights are set to be released soon.

en.title: 10.12–10.19 | This Week's Top AI Papers
en.summary: This week’s 10 selected frontier AI papers span quantum circuits, long-context agents, hybrid reasoning, multi-agent collaboration, RL training optimization, and more. The research introduces multiple novel frameworks that address pain points such as agent evidence drift, context redundancy, and high compute costs, with several approaches substantially reducing token consumption and improving reasoning accuracy. Breakthroughs also include AI-assisted quantum circuit design and distributed research agents, offering developers building agent systems, tuning large models, and exploring AI-driven scientific research a highly valuable frontier reference.

en.summary: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash gets a major update: with model pricing unchanged, it significantly boosts coding and tool-use capabilities, generating racing cars, Forbidden City 3D scenes, and interactive Godot game prototypes in one click. Software engineering and terminal task benchmark scores also climbed noticeably, and new Search and Fetch web-retrieval interfaces enable low-cost information lookup. Let's see how it performs.

en.title:
SIWITHUS 014 | When the entry-level ladder breaks first

This week, two things side by side: a New York report says that since ChatGPT launched, entry-level job postings in design, media, and writing are down about 40.6%, while postings requiring AI skills are up about 55%; in Anthropic’s own employment research, the share of junior technical hiring fell from 27% to 9%, and agent work hours to human hours are roughly 6 to 1.

en.title: Seeing so many people enjoy this game demo puts my mind at ease. That said, Codex+Unreal isn't the optimal solution—Unreal built a skill specifically for Claude Code, which gives Claude a higher development ceiling. We have hit some bottlenecks, though: LLMs can't handle Control Rig well, especially complex attack animations. Anyone got a good solution?
